Subject: Acme procurement: post-demo recap & next steps (PO vs Card / Marketplace)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on procurement readiness and the commercial path: 

What we discussed:
- Demo highlights: predictable p99 latency with Dedicated, prefix caching to reduce per-token cost, and private deployment options for regulated data.
- Commercial paths: 1) Purchase via PO (monthly bill + required SOW/contract), 2) Pay-by-card (self-serve, faster but limits on seat/commitment policies), 3) AWS Marketplace (can be the cleanest path if your procurement requires marketplace invoicing).
- Procurement blockers you called out: internal legal redlines on data residency, need for SOC2 evidence, and whether Acme requires a PO vs. marketplace invoice.

Next steps I propose:
1) I attach a draft SOW and our procurement instructions (see attachments). Please share with your procurement team to confirm PO requirements.
2) Ben will follow up with a short pricing reminder and card vs PO economics.
3) If Acme prefers marketplace, we can provision a marketplace quote and route the invoice that way — Dev, can you confirm estimated lead time for marketplace listing/quote?

Would love to sync mid-next-week after you talk to procurement. If PO is the path, can procurement confirm the contact and the expected PO issuance timeline?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Hey Marissa —

Appreciate the recap and the SOW. A few quick notes from procurement: 

- Acme typically prefers PO for any committed spend > $25k/year. Card is ok for pilots under that threshold.
- Marketplace is preferred by our vendor management team because it simplifies invoicing and terms acceptance, but some cost centers cannot buy from marketplace due to internal chargeback rules.
- We need SOC2 Type II evidence and a short data residency appendix for our legal team.

Questions for you: 
1) If we go PO, can your billing team accept net-30?
2) If we go marketplace, how long to produce a marketplace quote and get it live (we may need it for approvals)?

I'll loop in procurement directly on their availability — they want the draft SOW and a short note on billing terms to start the internal approval.

Best,
Alex

Hi Alex / Procurement team —

Following up with the specific answers you asked for: 

1) Billing terms: We can accept net-30 on PO for committed annual contracts. For pilots (month-to-month) we typically ask for card payment. If you need net-45/60 we can escalate to finance but would need a business justification.

2) Marketplace timing: Typical lead time to get a quote visible is 7–10 business days once we confirm SOW and pricing. We can prioritize if Acme is ready to proceed.

3) SOC2 / data residency: Laura from legal is copied and can provide SOC2 artifacts and a short data residency appendix. Laura — can you share the SOC2 package and a draft appendix?

I've also attached our pricing schedule and a one-page procurement checklist that includes PO routing examples and what to include in the invoice reference to speed processing.

Next practical step: Alex / procurement, which path would you prefer we prepare first — (A) PO + net-30 quote + SOW, or (B) Marketplace quote? If you confirm A, we'll issue a formal quote and a ready-to-sign SOW. If B, we'll push the marketplace flow and share the marketplace quote link as soon as it's live.

Thanks,
